title: Mirror
vs Photo

post.title: Why You Hate Photos of Yourself #shorts
post.description: Mirror or photo: which one looks like you? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend who untags everything. Rosa sees the group photo and wants it deleted: her face looks wrong. In 'Reversed Facial Images and the Mere-Exposure Hypothesis' (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1977), Theodore Mita, Marshall Dermer and Jeffrey Knight printed women's photos twice, as they really look and mirror-reversed. The women preferred their mirror image; their close friends preferred the true one. We like the face we see most, and you mostly see yours in a mirror: the mere exposure effect. Your face isn't wrong in photos. It's just the right way round. #psychology #shorts #mereexposure #selfie #overthinking

lines.say: In nineteen seventy-seven, women's photos were printed true and mirrored.
lines.text: In 1977, women's photos were printed true and MIRRORED.
Women picked their mirror image. Friends picked the TRUE one.
We like the face we see MOST: mere exposure.
Think of the last photo you untagged. Yeah, THAT one.
